Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Follow all instructions provided by election officials
Situation2: Officials ask voters with last names A–M to move to a newly opened line, even though the original line is moving faster.
Story:
I stood in the crowded community center, clutching my phone in one hand and my voter ID in the other. The line for voting snaked around the room, and I could hear the buzz of conversation—some people grumbling, others chatting about the upcoming holiday. My daughter had just texted, reminding me that the family video call was about to start. It was our tradition to reconnect before the holiday, sharing stories and laughter, and I knew how much my grandkids looked forward to seeing me on the screen.

Just then, an election official called out, “If your last name starts with A through M, please move to the new line on the left.” I glanced at the new line; it was longer and barely moving. The original line, where I’d been waiting, was finally picking up speed. I hesitated. The rules were clear, and I wanted to set a good example as a responsible citizen. But if I switched lines, I’d miss the call, disappointing my family and breaking our tradition. My heart pounded as I weighed the expectations—my family’s need for connection against my duty to follow the voting process.
